newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALY LIKELY TO CHANGE AGAIN FOR GEORGIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALY LIKELY TO CHANGE AGAIN FOR GEORGIA.

text.p: Italian coach Arrigo Sacchi is likely to return to his favoured 4-4-2 line-up for Italy's World Cup group two qualifier against Georgia in Perugia on Wednesday after their unconvincing 3-1 win over Moldova on Saturday.
Although Italy won the team's overall performance satisfied neither critics nor Sacchi.

Under pressure to produce a more convincing performance in his first home game since this summer's European Championship failure, Sacchi intends to abandon the three man attack of Fabrizio Ravanelli, Pierluigi Casiraghi and Enrico Chiesa used initially against Moldova.

"We were not much of a side against Moldova but I had to try out a new scheme even if I knew it was a risk. Anyway, on the eve of the Moldova game I said that I would change things around if it didn't work out", Sacchi told reporters.
Sacchi is expected to drop Chiesa, bringing in Juventus midfielder Angelo Di Livio, impressive as a second half substitute against Moldova.
The Italian coach may also ring the changes in defence, dropping the out of form AC Milan defender Alessandro Costacurta to make way for new cap -- Juventus defender Gianluca Pessotto.
When Sacchi gave a first cap to Alessandro Nesta on Saturday, the Lazio defender became the 52nd debutant of the five year Sacchi era.

Italy (probable team): Francesco Toldo, Gianluca Pessotto, Paolo Maldini, Ciro Ferrara, Alessandro Nesta; Angelo Di Livio, Roberto Di Matteo, Antonio Conte, Amedeo Carboni; Pierluigi Casiraghi, Fabrizio Ravanelli
